en: The *Buddhabhāṣita-saddharmopāya-dhāraṇī-sūtra*.
The translator’s name is lost; it is now appended to the Catalogue of the Eastern Jin.
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Buddha was dwelling at the site of the Bodhi-maṇḍala in the realm of Magadha.
Beneath the *tī* tree,
he was gathered together with a great assembly of bhikṣus,
among whom were those named the Greatly Wise Śāriputra and others.
The Elder Maudgalyāyana, the Elder Ānanda,
and other great śrāvakas.
And the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas,
including Vajradhvaja Bodhisattva and Vajragarbha Bodhisattva.
Maitreya Bodhisattva and the assembly of great bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of this Bhadrakalpa—
then the Vajradhara deity addressed the Buddha, saying:
The World-Honored One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha,
truly knows and sees this light and majestic power of the dhāraṇī-mantra of skillful means,
which has the capacity to destroy all evils.
It provides protection for those who have no protection.
Even if they encounter any evil conditions, bad associates,
venomous dragons, various ghosts, yakṣas, or rākṣasas.
Furthermore, many *kumbhāṇḍas*, humans, non-humans,
and others shall not fear swords, staves, enemies, or sudden calamities;
nor shall they be able to disturb them through malevolent spirits, sorcery, or incantations.
Even when engaged in the four modes of conduct— walking, standing, sitting, or lying down— they do not abandon sentient beings;
just as I now attend upon the Tathāgata without ever being separated from him for even a moment,
so too shall this dhāraṇī be present at all times.
To protect and benefit sentient beings,
never abandoning them from the very beginning is likewise so.
Therefore, I now entreat the Tathāgata to proclaim this dhāraṇī.
This dhāraṇī is itself the bodhisattva; it is itself the Mahāyāna.
Why is this? If there are sons or daughters of good family who are without protection, this [dhāraṇī] can provide them with protection.
Because it completely extinguishes all strife, litigation, bondage, and various injustices.
At that time, the Buddha said to the Vajrapāṇi deity:
"Excellent, excellent, Vajrapāṇi! It is just as you have said."

It is because you are thus able to exhort the Tathāgata for the sake of sentient beings that I shall now listen attentively as I explain for you the dhāraṇī mantra of skillful means for wholesome dharmas.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke this mantra:
*U-kau (1) Mau-kau (2) Ma-vi-ni (3) Ma-ta-ni (4) Pa-ra-cha-le (5) Na-hiu hiu-li yue-tuo (6) Svāhā*. Then the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha—
Having spoken this "Dhāraṇī of the Victorious King of the Majestic Great Crown," he addressed Vajrapāṇi:
"You should thus recollect and uphold it."
The Tathāgata shall now speak further for you.
He then spoke this mantra:
*vase rai* (1) *vase rai* (2) *vase rai dhare* (3) *vase rai bhate* (4).
1. Vatsale vidi 2. Vatsale datti 3. Jvālara vatsale 4.
Jvālaradharī 5. Dhare 6. Dhare 7. Vare 8. Mūre 9. Chare 10. Hūhūre 11. Phaṅga 12. Vivilī 13. Ririśi
17. *Līśrī*, 18. *Lūlūci*, 19. *Cale*, 20. *Cūle*, 21.
*Mūle*, 22. *Maṇḍale*, 23. *Sapopivisadhu*, 24. *Cicudhupire*, 25. *Mālai*, 26. *Hātani*. 27. [Omitted].
Vare (28) Vare (29) Vadi (30) Vadhi (31) Vidhe (32) Vire (33) Lūsare (34) Śarave (35) Rasane (36) Ropana-leye (37) Māṅku.
Cchalina (38), Indravati (39), Titiroya (40), namo maheśvarāya ni (41), liśiṃ-ba-vani (42), pāpācampāni (43), kharapati (44), bhūtapati (45).
45. *Sakhīke* (Sakhī, with the *zhū* reversed as *xié*) 46. *Somavati* 47.
*Somāṅge svāhā* 48. The Buddha addressed Vajrapāṇi:
I shall further explain to you a divine mantra that enables the practitioner to attain long life in the present life.
He then spoke the mantra, saying:
1. *Hara*, 2. *hara*, 3. *khira*. At that time, Vajrapāṇi addressed the Buddha, saying:
"So be it, World-Honored One; I shall receive and uphold [this mantra].

4. *Kaṭṭa*, 5. *paṭṭa*, 6. *ayina*, 7. *haricampāni*, 8. *kakkatani*, 9. *addha* (with the tongue rolled back), 10. *ahani*, 11. *maghavilohani*, 12. *husavade*, 13. *pusavade*, 14. *hiri* (pronounced with the *ri* sound), 15. *hiri*, 16. *yathaśe*, 17. *yathakiṇi*, 18. *yathapalañca*, 19. *yathabhañja*, 20. *yathakidabhañja*. Having spoken this mantra, he addressed Vajrapāṇi."
Thus has this Dharma-dhāraṇī mantra been spoken by the Tathāgata for the benefit of all sentient beings and out of great compassion.
I shall now speak it further for you,
just as the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha of the past spoke this sublime teaching—
a truth confirmed by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present, which is sincere and not false.
At that time, the World-Honored One immediately emitted light from the mark between his eyebrows,
illuminating all buddha-fields. Wherever this light shone, it universally benefited immeasurable sentient beings.
When the Buddhas of those directions saw this light,
they each rose from their seats and, following the light together, came to the Sahā world.
Having arrived in this land, they praised it with one voice, saying:
Excellent, World-Honored One Śākyamuni, you have skillfully entrusted [this teaching] for the benefit,
welfare, and happiness of all sentient beings.
Excellent, excellent, Śākyamuni Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha!
For the sake of benefiting all sentient beings;
for their protection and shelter; for illumination;
and to cause sentient beings to attain joy.
"This Dharani-mantra of wholesome dharmas has been spoken;
the phrases spoken by us Buddhas are likewise all thus.
Excellent, Śākyamuni, you who are able to bestow [benefits] extensively!"
If any son of good family or daughter of good family hears this dhāraṇī mantra of the wholesome dharma and desires to obtain its benefits,
they should receive, uphold, read, and recite it at dawn.
We shall immediately protect those among us who are Buddhas.
Wherever this mantra is recited and maintained, that place will be auspicious,
for we Buddhas all abide therein.
If all sentient beings have previously committed extremely grave evil karmas,
these shall all be extinguished without remainder,
thereby enabling these sons of good family [to attain such results].
One will fully obtain twenty benefits:
first, one attains longevity in the present life;
second, one's dwelling becomes peaceful and secure.
Third, one's reputation will be heard far and wide;
fourth, one will attain honor and nobility in the present life;
fifth, one will possess abundant wealth and treasures.
Sixth, his majestic appearance is preeminent;
seventh, he is courageous and fearless;
eighth, he is free from all diseases.
Ninth, peace and happiness;
tenth, advancing without weariness;
eleventh, being protected and remembered by all Buddhas.
Twelfth, they are protected by the devas.
Thirteenth, they are loved and respected by all people.
Fourteenth, they see the Buddhas face-to-face.
Fifteenth, they are protected by virtuous friends.
Sixteenth, they are not subjected to poisonous harm.
Seventeenth, evil spirits are subdued.
18. Enemies will naturally vanish.
19. One’s retinue will be perfected.
20. Noble aspirations will be fulfilled according to one’s heart.
Thus, O Vajradhara, this dhāraṇī mantra is the locus of the subtle and secret treasury of all Buddhas,
and it is that which all Buddhas protect and keep in mind.
"It is true, not false, subtle, and well-spoken.
At that time, the Vajradhara deity addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, regarding this divine mantra spoken by the Tathāgata..."
One should likewise rejoice in it, believe in it with delight, and proclaim it.
Why is this? Because of the power of this dhāraṇī mantra, those who have no protection can find protection.
Because it brings great benefit,
for the sake of such sons and daughters of good family as these,
I shall now further expound the dhāraṇī-mantra of the wholesome dharma.
Those who desire peace and happiness, as well as those seeking liberation,
should receive, uphold, read, and recite this at dawn;
they shall then obtain the power of protection from the divine mantra.
"You shall certainly be forever freed from all suffering and affliction.
He then spoke this mantra:

Śiri (1), Śiri (2), Chi-ti (3), Chi-ti (4), Po-po (5), Po-po (6), Lo-lo (7), Lo-lo (8), Shi-shi (9), Shi-shi (10), Ka-ra (11), Ka-ra (12), Ā-hi (13), Ā-hi (14), Pho-p'o (15), Pho-p'o (16), Mo-hsieh (17), Mo-hsieh (18), Ho-na (19), Ho-na (20), Ho-na (21), To-ho (22), To-ho (23), To-ho (24), Po-ch'e (25), Po-ch'e (26), Svāhā (27). At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Vajrapāṇi.
Excellent, excellent, O Vajrapāṇi!
This dhāraṇī is most divine and most efficacious;
it is for the sake of all sentient beings that I have spoken it.
By the majestic power of this dhāraṇī mantra,
it is able to completely shield every single pore,
causing all nāgas, ghosts, and every kind of pestilence to be obstructed.
No evil or poisonous vapors can enter it,
and it can also act as a causal condition for liberation.
At that time, Mahābrahmā, the Lord of the Trichiliocosm, [spoke].
He immediately rose from his seat, prostrated before the Buddha, joined his palms toward the Buddha, and addressed him, saying:
"Excellent, World-Honored One! I too now delight in praising, rejoicing in, benefiting, and accomplishing [this teaching]."
"Good sons who practice this mantra should,
at dawn, receive, uphold, read, and recite this dhāraṇī,
just as the World-Honored One now does for the sake of benefiting, bringing peace to, and protecting such sentient beings."
When this *dhāraṇī* mantra of the wholesome dharmas was being spoken, the Great Brahmā King immediately spoke the mantra, saying:
1. *jili* 2. *mili* 3. *cili svāhā* 4. *dṛṃma-phuri svāhā* 5. *dṛṃma-ḍi svāhā* 6. *pake-ḍi* 7. *phupha-saṃtari svāhā* Having spoken this mantra, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
The dhāraṇī mantra thus spoken by the Great Virtuous and Most Honored One can provide complete protection for these good sons and good daughters,
and can also cause them to increase their lifespan.
Therefore, practitioners should, at dawn, read, recite, practice, and uphold it according to the Dharma.
At that time, Śakra Devānām Indra again addressed the Buddha, saying:
World-Honored One, I too now desire to benefit and protect such sons of good family.
Those who recite this dhāraṇī shall be protected and remembered by all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones.
Therefore, if a practitioner wishes to obtain the merit and benefits of this dhāraṇī mantra,
they should read, recite, receive, and uphold it at dawn.
At that time, Śakra spoke the mantra as follows:

Vini-varaṇe (1) bhada-mārate (2) ci-ci-ci (3) kuli-kandari (4) mara-mara-pa (5) hana-mata-dhāraṇi (6) dhāra-malini (7) cakra-phaṭ (8) śambhali (9) śambhari svāhā (10). At that time, there were also the four great heavenly kings: the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa, the Heavenly King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the Heavenly King Virūḍhaka, and the Heavenly King Virūpākṣa.
With palms joined in reverence, they addressed the Buddha, saying:
"We, the Four Kings, shall likewise protect these sons and daughters of good family who delight in practicing this skillful means *dhāraṇī*."
Those sentient beings should likewise receive, uphold, read, and recite it at dawn.
At that time, the Four Kings spoke these mantras:
*Phuba 1, śubhaphaba 2, dhūmāparihārai 3, ariparaseṭi 4, śaṇṭe 5, nemuṭe 6, mogale 7, ḍuṭe ḍuṭe svāhā 8-9*. At that time, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni...
He then raised his right hand and addressed Śakra Devendra, Mahābrahmā, and the four World Protectors:
"Excellent, excellent, O Great Virtuous Devas! It is well that you are able to rejoice in and proclaim this King of Dharanis of Skillful Means for the Good Dharma."
These dhāraṇīs of wholesome dharmas are all protected and remembered by all Buddhas;
you should always properly receive and uphold them.
At that time, the World-Honored One again addressed the Vajrapāṇi deity:
"Excellent, excellent, Vajrapāṇi!
This is a skillful means and the attainment of the long-life dhāraṇī mantra."
These three mantras are all protected,
praised, and authenticated by the Tathāgatas, the Buddhas of the ten directions;
they are guarded by the celestial kings and the great powerful spirits and deities.
If sons or daughters of good family who wish to practice this path should first purify their own body, speech, and mind.
If, at the time of dawn, one receives and maintains [the precepts] with a sincere and respectful mind,
and recites them with a pure heart according to the Dharma—
one who can do so will not be seen by devas, nāgas, or various evil humans and ghosts.
Should anyone be able to inflict harm and find an opportunity against him,
at that time the Bodhisattva, the great assembly of śrāvakas,
the Vajrapāṇi deities, the various heavenly kings, all ghosts and spirits, nāga kings, yakṣas, humans, non-humans, and so forth [will protect him].
All together paid respectful homage, were filled with great joy, and received, upheld, and practiced it.
Thus concludes the *Sūtra on the Dhāraṇī of Skillful Means of the Good Dharma* spoken by the Buddha.
